findings.title: Recovery-code login form crashes when the credential lives only in user storage
findings.body: After this change, recovery codes can be stored only in user storage (updateCredential returns true, so no local credential is written). The login form still does RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) and immediately calls Optional.get() / createFromCredentialModel. getCredential only sees a federated credential if the storage provider overrides CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials(); the SPI default is an empty stream, and a stored raw JSON blob is not a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel. configuredFor can still be true via isConfiguredFor, so the authenticator runs and rendering the challenge throws NoSuchElementException or a JSON parse error. Users whose storage follows the existing OTP pattern (updateCredential / isValid / isConfiguredFor only) cannot open the recovery-code page.

findings.title: Successful federated recovery-code login is treated as an exhausted credential
findings.body: On a valid code the authenticator now loads the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential. If that Optional is empty — the normal case when user storage accepted the credential but does not return a full RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel — recoveryCodeCredentialModel stays null and the code unconditionally adds CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES. Every successful use of a user-storage recovery code therefore forces the user through setup again, even when codes remain. If getCredentials returns a non-conforming model, createFromCredentialModel throws and a code that already validated still fails the flow.

findings.title: Last federated recovery code is never removed
findings.body: When the reloaded model reports allCodesUsed(), the authenticator calls removeStoredCredentialById. That API deletes only local DB credentials. A federated credential id is not found there, so the call is a no-op and the exhausted credential stays configured in user storage (isConfiguredFor remains true). The test storage makes this worse: getCredentials rebuilds the model with RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues, which does not copy the id assigned in updateCredential, so even a federated-aware delete would target the wrong id. Users keep being prompted for codes that can no longer succeed, or keep an exhausted factor alongside the reconfigure required action.

findings.title: User-storage recovery codes are cleartext and never consumed
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential JSON-serializes the raw code list into UserCredentialModel's challenge and hands it to updateCredential, discarding the already-hashed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel used for local storage. Nothing in the success path writes an updated set back after isValid. Local codes are single-use only because RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid removes the used hash and saves the credential; that provider is skipped when user storage returns true. The payload is a static JSON array with no used-flag, stored by the new test provider in credentialData (the non-secret field) and checked with anyMatch against every code. A storage compromise yields immediately usable codes, and the same code can be replayed until the set is replaced. Persist the hashed model (or an equivalent remaining-code structure), and consume the presented code inside the storage isValid implementation.

findings.title: Test user storage accepts any recovery code and cannot revoke them
findings.body: isValid deserializes the stored list and returns true if any entry equals the challenge. It does not require the next unused code and does not delete the code it accepted, so the integration test's single login cannot catch replay. disableCredentialType only clears OTP and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream only advertises OTP, so admin or account disable of recovery-authn-codes logs 'Unsupported' and leaves recoveryCodes set. getCredentials also NPEs if getMyUser returns null, and on success rebuilds a model from the original full list, so the code number never advances. This is the only storage implementation of the new contract, and it does not enforce single-use or revocation.
